page: Google Cloud Platform c2d-highcpu-16 is a compute-optimized server instance featuring 16 vCPUs and 32 GB of RAM, configured on the x86_64 architecture. Powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor, this instance provides 8 physical cores with 2 threads per core under a dedicated CPU allocation model. The hardware configuration includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, alongside hardware support for AVX, AES, VAES, and SHA_NI cryptographic instructions. It does not include local storage or bundled GPUs.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong single-core CPU capabilities, with stress-ng single-core performance ranking in the top 25%. Multi-core performance and memory bandwidth benchmarks, such as the Passmark memory score, show average to strong results, with read-only large block memory bandwidth reaching 80.47 GB/sec. The instance also demonstrates strong text generation speeds for small language models at 301.82 tokens/sec, while maintaining average performance in software compilation, ray tracing, and database operations.

From a resource density perspective, the 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio makes this instance a cost-efficient option for compute-heavy workloads that do not require massive memory footprints. The dedicated AMD EPYC processor cores ensure predictable execution times, though the lack of local NVMe storage requires external disk attachment. This server is suited for workloads such as software compilation, web serving, lightweight LLM inference, and compute-bound batch processing.
